subject: 5 deal-killers we catch the most
preheader: the patterns that show up in bad deals over and over.
headline: Five things TrueCap flags in bad deals — and most amateur underwriting misses.
body: After thousands of address analyses, the same five problems show up over and over in deals investors were about to buy. Watch for these on the next property you run.

One: reassessed property tax. Seller's tax bill reflects the old assessment. When you buy at today's price, the county resets your assessment and your tax bill jumps 20-40%. Texas and Florida are the worst for this. Always model the post-sale tax bill, not the seller's bill.

Two: insurance set at last year's rate. Premiums are rising 10-15% per year nationally, 25-50% in coastal Florida and parts of Texas. Underwriting with a stale quote means year-two NOI evaporates. Get a fresh quote before you close.

Three: rent comps using listed rents instead of leased rents. Listed rents on Zillow and Apartments.com run 8-12% above what units actually rent for after concessions. Use the lower end of the range, not the median asking price.

Four: PM fees modeled at 8% with no leasing fee. The real all-in PM cost is closer to 11-13% once you add lease-up, renewals, maintenance markups, and admin. Underestimating PM is a $1,000+/yr NOI mistake on a typical property.
Five: DSCR that only works at base-case rent. The lender's floor is 1.20-1.25. If your deal is at 1.22 and rents drop 5% in a soft market, you've blown the covenant. Build a buffer or pass.
